docs.title: SoulStore
docs.text: SoulStore is a server-side Luau module for Roblox with per-session DataStore ownership and a path-based API.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Description Session ownership GUID tokens distinguish sessions even within the same server. Lifecycle Pending and ending souls are unavailable for gameplay. Autosave Shared scheduling saves Active souls in the background, spread evenly, with everyone getting a turn when the budget is tight. Safe saves A stray key or an odd table cannot wipe out a save, and nothing in it is quietly lost. Serialized finalization Final save and unlock happen atomically after any current writer. Data API Nested paths, change listeners, reconciliation, and load/save hooks. Shutdown Cancels pending work and retries final saves within a bounded budget.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Build the Rojo project with rojo build -o SoulStore.rbxlx, or install the Wally package. Require SoulStore from a server Script.

local SoulStore = require(path.to.SoulStore)
local DEFAULT_DATA = { Coins = 0, Level = 1 }

game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    -- The second argument is the DataStore scope. nil uses Roblox's default.
    local soul = SoulStore.new("PlayerData", nil, player, DEFAULT_DATA)
    if not soul then return end

    local loaded, reason = soul:LoadData()
    if not loaded then
        warn("Player data unavailable:", reason)
        return
    end

    soul:Reconcile(DEFAULT_DATA)
    soul:SetData({ "Coins" }, soul:GetData({ "Coins" }) + 50)
end)

Read Getting Started for integration and Session Locking for lifecycle, crash recovery, and rollout guidance. Never start gameplay on a pending soul or use defaults when loading fails.

Server only

DataStoreService is unavailable on the client. Require SoulStore only from server code.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Require SoulStore only from server code.

For Rojo, clone the repository, run rojo build -o SoulStore.rbxlx, and copy the SoulStore module from ServerScriptService into your project.

For Wally, add soulstore = "mystifine/soulstore@2.0.2" to your project's server dependencies, then run wally install. If your game already uses 1.x, read Migrating from 1.x first, because some arguments changed.

local SoulStore = require(path.to.SoulStore)

docs.title: Player lifecycle
docs.text:
Keep the default schema in a shared server module. Create one soul per exact Player instance and DataStore, and start gameplay only after a successful load.

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local SoulStore = require(path.to.SoulStore)
local DEFAULT_DATA = {
    Stats = { Gold = 0, Gems = 0 },
    Inventory = {},
}

local function onPlayerAdded(player)
    -- Avoid repeating this service's own initialization during startup races.
    if SoulStore.getPendingSoul("PlayerData", nil, player)
        or SoulStore.hasActiveSession("PlayerData", nil, player)
        or SoulStore.getEndingSoul("PlayerData", nil, player) then
        return
    end
    -- The second argument is the DataStore scope. nil uses Roblox's default.
    local soul = SoulStore.new("PlayerData", nil, player, DEFAULT_DATA)
    if not soul then return end

    soul:SetOnLoad(function(data)
        -- Migrate the argument directly; soul gameplay methods are unavailable here.
        if data.Stats == nil then
            data.Stats = { Gold = 0, Gems = 0 }
        end
    end)

    local loaded, reason = soul:LoadData()
    if not loaded then
        warn("Could not initialize player data:", reason)
        return
    end

    soul:Reconcile(DEFAULT_DATA)
    -- Start gameplay and replication here, after confirmed ownership.
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
    task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, player)
end

SoulStore caches pending work immediately and shares concurrent loads. Application startup should still be wired once, so your own gameplay initialization is not repeated.

SoulStore handles PlayerRemoving and BindToClose automatically. A departing Player's soul is cancelled if still Pulling, or final-saved if Active. A rejoining Player gets a fresh soul and waits for the old session to release its lock.

For later gameplay requests, look up the current session:

local function awardGold(player, amount)
    local soul = SoulStore.getSoul("PlayerData", nil, player)
    if not soul then return end
    local gold = soul:GetData({ "Stats", "Gold" })
    soul:SetData({ "Stats", "Gold" }, gold + amount)
end

Validate all client-originating requests on the server before using data APIs. Replicate only the gameplay fields the client needs; keep session metadata on the server.

docs.title: Replication example
docs.text:
SoulStore does not create remotes. If your project has a GetPlayerData RemoteFunction in ReplicatedStorage, its server handler can expose an explicit gameplay snapshot:

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local getPlayerData = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("GetPlayerData")

getPlayerData.OnServerInvoke = function(player)
    local soul = SoulStore.getSoul("PlayerData", nil, player)
    if not soul then return nil end
    return {
        Stats = SoulStore.deepCopy(soul:GetData({ "Stats" })),
        Inventory = SoulStore.deepCopy(soul:GetData({ "Inventory" })),
    }
end

The client should keep its loading UI visible when no Active data is available. Request again through your game's readiness flow after initialization; do not replace an unavailable response with a default profile.

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local getPlayerData = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("GetPlayerData")
local data = getPlayerData:InvokeServer()
if data then
    -- Initialize the player's data UI from this confirmed snapshot.
end

For later changes, have trusted server gameplay call SetData and send the resulting field through your own RemoteEvent. OnDataChanged can drive those deltas. Clients should request actions such as buying an item; the server validates them and decides the data mutation.

docs.title: Readiness and failure handling
docs.text:
LoadData returns true only for Active data. Failed loads, pending locks, and terminal sessions must not enter gameplay. Do not publish a loaded marker, send a default profile to the client, or grant rewards before successful loading.

getSoul returns only Active sessions. Use getPendingSoul and getEndingSoul for inspection. SessionState describes the lifecycle; LoadState is a compatibility status.

React to SessionEndBindableEvent if your game should disconnect or move a player out of gameplay after ownership loss. SoulStore does not kick players automatically. Check EndReason for outcomes such as Saved, OwnershipLost, Cancelled, AcquisitionUncertain, SaveRejected, CorruptData, HookFailed, DataStoreError, or InternalError.

Check the boolean result of manual SaveData calls when a confirmed write matters. A normal save makes one attempt, so false means it did not land; try again or wait for the next autosave. Session completion also includes cancellation and ownership loss, so a terminal event alone is not proof of a successful final save.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Edit src/Config.luau before deployment.

Setting Default Purpose DEBUG_MODE true Routine output, such as each load and save. Persistence warnings always show, even when this is off. TRACE_BACK_MESSAGE false Append stack traces to diagnostics. LOAD_ATTEMPT_INTERVAL 6 seconds Delay between looks at a lock that a load is waiting for. RETRY_INTERVAL 2 seconds First delay before a failed load or final save retries. MAX_RETRY_INTERVAL 30 seconds Longest delay that failed loads slow down to after repeated failures. MAX_FINAL_SAVE_RETRY_INTERVAL 10 seconds Longest delay between final save attempts. Shorter than loads, so a final save reaches the store first. AUTO_SAVE_INTERVAL 30 seconds Background save scheduling interval. SESSION_EXPIRY 120 seconds How long a lock can go without a write before another session may take it. TAKEOVER_DELAY 15 seconds How long a load waits on a lock past the expiry, taking it only if it has not changed. Set from MAX_FINAL_SAVE_RETRY_INTERVAL, so it is longer than a final save's slowest retry. HUNG_SAVE_TIME 60 seconds How long a save can run before it no longer holds up the next one. WRITER_WAIT_TIMEOUT 10 seconds Longest a save waits behind one already running. ACQUISITION_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT 30 seconds Retry window for releasing a cancelled acquisition with an uncertain response.

The shared autosave scheduler checks Active souls once per second. Each player's autosaves are spread over the whole interval, a backlog is cleared at no more than twice the steady rate, and when the request budget cannot cover everyone, whoever has waited longest goes first. Normal saves make one attempt. Failed loads slow down to MAX_RETRY_INTERVAL and final saves to MAX_FINAL_SAVE_RETRY_INTERVAL, except during shutdown, when both stop slowing down at three times RETRY_INTERVAL. Each wait varies by 20% either way, so players and servers do not retry at the same moment.

Keep the expiry comfortably longer than autosaves and expected request delays. Shutdown keeps the server up until every session has settled, for as long as Roblox allows, which is 30 seconds. It cannot guarantee successful writes during an outage.

Before deploying this lifecycle update, drain old servers. Existing data does not need migration, but older pending writes cannot enforce the new per-session token model. See Session Locking, and Migrating from 1.x if your game already uses SoulStore.

docs.title: Soul Methods
docs.text: A soul belongs to one exact Player instance and DataStore. Gameplay access requires an Active session. Use getSoul for readiness checks. A session starts ending as soon as its player leaves. An outage does not end a session: it stays Active, and its next save lands once the store is back.

docs.title: :LoadData()
docs.text:
soul:LoadData() -> (boolean, string?)

Yields until ownership is acquired and SetOnLoad completes, or loading stops. Returns true only when the soul is Active; otherwise returns false and a reason. Concurrent callers wait for the same load rather than issuing duplicate acquisitions.

Foreign locks and transient DataStore errors retry while the player remains present. Defaults are written only for a missing record. Malformed existing data, including a record stored as an array, is never replaced with defaults: the load stops with CorruptData and the record is left as it is. Leaving or shutdown cancels pending work. A confirmed acquisition after cancellation is released without starting gameplay. If the response is uncertain, bounded recovery tries to release only this token; an unresolved lock relies on expiry.

local soul = SoulStore.new("PlayerData", nil, player, DEFAULT_DATA)
if not soul then return end
local loaded, reason = soul:LoadData()
if not loaded then
    warn("Player data unavailable:", reason)
    return
end
print("Coins:", soul:GetData({ "Coins" }))

docs.title: :SaveData(sessionEnding?)
docs.text:
soul:SaveData(sessionEnding: boolean?) -> (boolean, string?)

With false or no argument, saves an Active soul, increments SaveId, refreshes LastUpdate, and retains ownership. It makes one attempt, waiting first behind any save already running. Returns true for a confirmed write; rejected or unavailable operations return false and a reason. A failed attempt is not retried, because the next autosave carries newer data anyway.

With true, immediately transitions to Ending, captures the final snapshot, and stops gameplay access. The final writer waits behind an in-flight save, then writes data and unlocks in the same UpdateAsync. It retries until the write lands, another session owns the record, or an error occurs that retrying cannot fix, in which case the lock is released without the final data. Repeated end requests coalesce; an end request received while finalization is running may return false, "Ending". Observe SessionEndBindableEvent or terminal state for completion.

Foreign or missing ownership is never overwritten or reported as a successful save. Ending a Pulling soul cancels loading instead of saving its defaults. Called from inside a load or save hook, it returns false, "CalledFromHook". See Lifecycle Hooks.

local saved, reason = soul:SaveData()
if not saved then warn("Save not confirmed:", reason) end
-- Normally automatic on PlayerRemoving and shutdown:
soul:SaveData(true)

docs.title: :GetData(path?)
docs.text:
soul:GetData(path: {string | number}?) -> any?

Returns a nested value, or the full data table when the path is omitted. Returns nil outside Active, for a missing key, or when traversal encounters a non-table.

local coins = soul:GetData({ "Coins" })
local level = soul:GetData({ "Stats", "Level" })
local item = soul:GetData({ "Inventory", 1 })

Table results remain live references for compatibility. Direct mutation bypasses state guards and listeners, so prefer SetData. The final snapshot is captured when Ending starts; later changes through retained references do not affect it.

docs.title: :SetData(path, value)
docs.text:
soul:SetData(path: {string | number}, value: any) -> any?

Sets a value and notifies path listeners. Returns the assigned value, or nil on rejection. Requires an Active soul, a nonempty path, and existing intermediate tables. MetaData is reserved for SoulStore.

Values a DataStore cannot hold are rejected: functions, threads, Instances and other Roblox types, strings that are not valid UTF-8, table keys that are not strings or numbers, and tables that contain themselves. NaN is rejected as well, because it is always a bug and would replace a good value. If one of these reaches the data through a direct table write, it is left out of each save with a warning instead of failing the save, except NaN, which saves as it is, also with a warning.

So are writes a DataStore would change or lose: a number key on a table with string keys, including the top of the save, a string key on an array, a number key that is not a whole number from 1, any number key but 1 on a table that is not an array yet, and a value with any of these inside it. See What can be saved. Check the return value when granting something of value.

soul:SetData({ "Coins" }, 500)
soul:SetData({ "Stats", "Level" }, 10)
soul:SetData({ "Inventory" }, { "Sword", "Shield" })

docs.title: :Reconcile(data)
docs.text:
soul:Reconcile(data: {}?) -> nil

Recursively fills missing string keys on an Active soul without replacing existing values. An array the save already has is left as it is, and a missing one is copied whole. Newly inserted tables are copied; reserved metadata is excluded.

if soul:LoadData() then
    soul:Reconcile(DEFAULT_DATA)
end

Inside SetOnLoad, work directly on the callback argument; gameplay methods are unavailable before Active.

docs.title: :OnDataChanged(path, callback)
docs.text:
soul:OnDataChanged(
    path: {string | number}?,
    callback: (oldData: any?, newData: any?) -> nil
) -> { Disconnect: () -> nil }

Registers a listener for SetData changes. A listener on { "Stats" } also fires for { "Stats", "Level" }. It receives copies of the old and new values. Pass nil to observe the full data table. Call Disconnect() to unsubscribe. Listeners are cleaned up when the soul terminates. See Change Listeners.

docs.title: :SetOnLoad(callback)
docs.text:
soul:SetOnLoad(callback: (data: {}) -> nil) -> nil

Register before loading. Receives acquired data for validation or migration before Active. Mutate the argument directly. Hooks must not yield or modify MetaData.

A failed hook prevents gameplay. SoulStore releases ownership using the original acquired record, so partial migration changes are not saved.

soul:SetOnLoad(function(data)
    data.Coins = math.clamp(data.Coins or 0, 0, 1_000_000)
end)
local loaded, reason = soul:LoadData()

docs.title: :SetOnSave(callback)
docs.text:
soul:SetOnSave(callback: (snapshot: {}) -> nil) -> nil

Receives a copy of the save payload. Changes affect only that attempt, not live data. Hooks must not yield, modify MetaData, or perform non-idempotent side effects: they may run again on retries. Failed hooks do not commit their partial snapshots.

soul:SetOnSave(function(snapshot)
    snapshot.TempBoost = nil
end)

docs.title: Session completion
docs.text:
SessionEndBindableEvent.Event fires once with (state, reason) for terminal outcomes, including cancellation and ownership loss. The event and listeners are then destroyed. Connect before starting work; inspect SessionState and EndReason after completion instead of waiting for an event that already fired.

soul.SessionEndBindableEvent.Event:Connect(function(state, reason)
    print("Data session settled:", state, reason)
end)

Terminal state alone does not prove that a final save succeeded.

If another session takes the record, this session's next write is refused and it ends with EndReason == "OwnershipLost". SoulStore does not kick the player automatically; the owning service can react to the completion event.

docs.title: SoulStore.new()
docs.text:
SoulStore.new(datastoreId: string, scope: string?, player: Player, defaultData: {}) -> Soul?

Creates and caches a Pulling soul for the exact Player instance, DataStore, and scope. Repeated calls return its pending or active soul. A different Player instance with the same UserId gets a new object and GUID token. Ending or terminal objects are never reused.

scope selects the DataStore scope; nil uses Roblox's default, "global". Each scope holds separate records and separate sessions.

Returns nil for invalid arguments, a departed player, or shutdown, and for defaults that could not be saved: an array at the top, or anything SetData would refuse inside it. Defaults are copied and unavailable through gameplay methods until loading succeeds.

local soul = SoulStore.new("PlayerData", nil, player, { Coins = 0 })
if not soul then return end
if not soul:LoadData() then return end
soul:SetData({ "Coins" }, 100)

docs.title: Session lookups
docs.text:
SoulStore.getSoul(datastoreId: string, scope: string?, player: Player) -> Soul?
SoulStore.getPendingSoul(datastoreId: string, scope: string?, player: Player) -> Soul?
SoulStore.getEndingSoul(datastoreId: string, scope: string?, player: Player) -> Soul?
SoulStore.hasActiveSession(datastoreId: string, scope: string?, player: Player) -> boolean

All lookups use the exact Player instance, DataStore, and scope. getSoul returns only an Active soul; a session stops being Active as soon as its player leaves. Pending and ending helpers are for inspection; their data is unavailable for gameplay. Old-session cleanup cannot remove a new Player instance's soul.

docs.title: SoulStore.playerExists()
docs.text:
SoulStore.playerExists(player: Player?) -> boolean

Returns whether the argument is a Player currently parented to Players.

docs.title: SoulStore.getMetaData()
docs.text:
SoulStore.getMetaData(sessionToken: string?) -> SoulMetaData

Returns fresh metadata with SaveId = 0 and the current timestamp. Without a token, returns Locked = false, SessionId = "". With a token, returns locked metadata owned by that token. SessionId is opaque and does not identify a server JobId. Applications should not overwrite persisted metadata.

docs.title: SoulStore.deepCopy()
docs.text:
SoulStore.deepCopy(data: any?) -> any

Recursively copies tables, keeping each table's length and leaving metatables behind. Returns primitive values unchanged.

docs.title: SoulStore.output()
docs.text:
SoulStore.output(outputFunction: (any) -> any, ...: any) -> nil

Writes diagnostics using the supplied function, respecting DEBUG_MODE and TRACE_BACK_MESSAGE. Persistence warnings remain visible when verbose debug output is disabled.

docs.title: SoulStore.getDatastore()
docs.text:
SoulStore.getDatastore(datastoreId: string, scope: string?) -> DataStore

Returns the DataStore that SoulStore uses for that name and scope.

docs.title: SoulStore.resetData()
docs.text:
SoulStore.resetData(datastoreId: string, scope: string?, datastoreKey: string) -> boolean

Removes one DataStore key and returns whether it succeeded. Refused while this server has a session for that key. Sessions on other servers cannot be detected, so stop them first.

Data Loss

Deletes the saved profile. See Resetting Data.

SoulStore.resetData("PlayerData", nil, tostring(player.UserId))

docs.title: SoulStore.resetAllData()
docs.text:
SoulStore.resetAllData(datastoreId: string, scope: string?, confirmation: string?) -> boolean

Waits 10 seconds, lists all keys, then removes them sequentially. Returns whether every key was removed. Refused while this server has a session in that DataStore. Outside Studio, confirmation must repeat datastoreId or nothing is deleted. Stop sessions on other servers first.

Data Loss

Deletes every profile. See Resetting Data.

docs.title: SoulMetaData
docs.text:
Metadata persisted beside player data and managed by SoulStore:

export type SoulMetaData = {
    Locked: boolean,
    SaveId: number,
    LastUpdate: number,
    SessionId: string,
}
Field Meaning Locked A session owns the key. SaveId Save counter derived from the persisted record when saving. LastUpdate Unix timestamp refreshed by acquisition and saves. Lock age comes from Roblox's own timestamp for the key, so this is only a fallback. SessionId Opaque GUID session token, or "" when unlocked.

MetaData is reserved. game.JobId identifies a server, not its individual player sessions.

docs.title: Soul
docs.text:
A soul represents one DataStore session for one exact Player instance. Do not reassign identity properties.

Property Type Meaning DatastoreId string DataStore name. Scope string DataStore scope; "global" unless one was given. DatastoreKey string Persisted key, the UserId as a string. Player Player Exact Player instance. UserId number Immutable UserId used for the persisted key. SessionToken string Immutable GUID identifying this session. Data table Live data; use only while Active. LastAutoSave number When the last save started, in os.clock time. IsSaving boolean A save is in flight. SessionState string Authoritative lifecycle state. EndReason string? Reason the session settled. LoadState string Compatibility load status; use SessionState for readiness. SaveState string Compatibility save status. SessionEndBindableEvent BindableEvent Fires once with (state, reason), then is destroyed. 
Pulling -> Active -> Ending -> Ended
Pulling -> Cancelled

Pulling is pending acquisition or initialization. Active permits gameplay and autosaves. Ending blocks gameplay while finalization runs. Ended and Cancelled are terminal; never reuse those objects. A confirmed acquisition during cancellation is released before settlement. An uncertain acquisition receives bounded recovery attempts, then relies on stale-lock expiry if the service remains unavailable.

LoadData and SaveData return (boolean, string?). Terminal state alone does not prove a confirmed final save.

An outage does not end a session: it stays Active and keeps accepting changes, and its next save lands once the store is back. If another session takes the record, the next write is refused and the session ends with OwnershipLost. No automatic player kick occurs.

docs.title: The rules
docs.text:
One owner per record. Each session gets its own token, stored in MetaData.SessionId. A load may claim a record that is unlocked, already holds its own token, or has a lock past SESSION_EXPIRY that it has seen unchanged for TAKEOVER_DELAY. A lock that looks newer is still taken after watching it for all of SESSION_EXPIRY, in case this server's clock is slow. A save only asks whether the token is still its own. Locked and expiry never decide a save.

One lifecycle. SessionState is the only state that decides anything. Only an Active session can read or write.

Pulling -> Active -> Ending -> Ended
Pulling -> Cancelled

One writer at a time. IsSaving makes saves queue behind each other, so two writes for a session do not normally race. A save running for HUNG_SAVE_TIME no longer holds up the next, and only the newest write may land, so one that comes back late cannot undo a newer save.

An outage does not end a session. It stays Active and keeps accepting changes, and its next save lands once the store is back. A session only ends when its player leaves, its server shuts down, or a write finds that another session has taken the record. The token check is what stops an old session overwriting anything.

Fail closed. Refuse rather than guess: corrupt data is never replaced, a failed hook never writes, and a player waiting on a lock never plays on defaults.

One clock for each job. os.clock measures anything local, such as autosaves and how long a lock has gone unchanged, because it cannot jump. os.time only compares against Roblox's UpdatedTime, and is written as LastUpdate for older servers to read.

A table's shape is decided before Roblox sees it. Roblox stores a table with a length as an array that stops there, losing every other key. So a save never hands Roblox a table that would lose anything, SetData refuses to create one, and copies use table.clone, because rebuilding an array key by key can change its length. See DataValidator.removeUnstorable.

Nothing that waits starts inside a hook. A hook runs on its own thread, which is cancelled if it yields. A save or load started there would stop halfway with its session stranded, so isInsideHook refuses them, whichever soul they are for.

docs.title: Loading
docs.text:
Session.load runs acquireSession, which calls UpdateAsync until one of these happens:

Result What happens next Claimed finishAcquisition runs OnLoad, then makes the session Active. If the player left in the meantime, it releases the lock instead. Locked by someone else Waits LOAD_ATTEMPT_INTERVAL and tries again. Takes the lock over once it is past SESSION_EXPIRY and has looked the same for TAKEOVER_DELAY. That is longer than a final save's slowest retry, so an owner that outlived an outage reaches the record first. Request failed Waits with a growing delay and tries again, unless the error cannot be fixed by retrying. Restarts TAKEOVER_DELAY. Corrupt record Stops without touching it. Player left Cancels. If an earlier attempt may have taken the lock, it tries to release it for up to ACQUISITION_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
Normal save (Session.save). Used by autosave and SaveData(). Waits behind any running save, copies the data, runs OnSave on the copy, and makes one write. If it fails, the next autosave tries again.

Autosave (runSchedulerTick in init.luau). Runs once a second. Starts at most twice the steady rate and never more than the request budget, longest wait first, so that a backlog does not land in one frame, and a small budget still goes round everyone.

Final save (Session.finish). Used when leaving, at shutdown, and by SaveData(true). When a player leaves, it is deferred until every other PlayerRemoving handler has run, because Roblox runs the newest connection first and SoulStore's is one of the oldest. See When a player leaves.

  1. Copy the data and run OnSave right away, before anything can yield, so nothing that runs later can change what gets written. If the hook fails, make the copy again without it.
  2. Move to Ending, which blocks gameplay.
  3. Wait behind any running save.
  4. Write the data and unlock in the same UpdateAsync.
  5. Retry until the write lands, another session owns the record, or an error occurs that retrying cannot fix. In that last case the lock is released without the final data, so the player can rejoin on their last good save.

Retries start at RETRY_INTERVAL and grow to MAX_FINAL_SAVE_RETRY_INTERVAL. During shutdown they stop growing at three times RETRY_INTERVAL, because the server only has about 30 seconds.

writeRecord is the only place a save reaches the data store. Roblox may run a transform more than once, so it sets every metadata field from the record it was given rather than adding to a copy.

docs.title: Ending a session
docs.text: Session.settle is the one place a session ends. It sets the final state and reason, removes the soul from the cache, then fires SessionEndBindableEvent once and destroys it. Shutdown checks each session's state rather than counting those events, because a state cannot be missed or drift.

docs.title: Checking your changes
docs.text:
stylua src tests
selene src tests
lune run tests/lifecycle.luau
lune run tests/edgecases.luau
lune run tests/consumers.luau
lune run tests/games.luau
lune run tests/fakestore.luau
lune run tests/load.luau
rojo build --output SoulStore.rbxlx

.github/workflows/validate.yml runs all of these except tests/games.luau, which needs your games in sibling folders. The tests use a virtual clock and a fake data store. tests/studio/ has the probe that checks the fake data store against real ones, the end-to-end run of the real module, and a full server's worth of sessions on the real engine. Run them in a published test place before releasing. Load Testing has what the big runs found.

docs.title: Readiness
docs.text:
Only Active souls accept gameplay operations. Check the load result before making data available to the rest of the game:

local soul = SoulStore.new("PlayerData", nil, player, DEFAULT_DATA)
if not soul then return end
local loaded, reason = soul:LoadData()
if not loaded then return end
soul:Reconcile(DEFAULT_DATA)

For later lookups, use SoulStore.getSoul("PlayerData", nil, player). It returns only an Active soul for that exact Player instance.

docs.title: Path arrays
docs.text:
Paths are ordered string or number keys:

soul:GetData({ "Stats", "Level" })
soul:GetData({ "Inventory", 1 })
soul:GetData() -- full live table

Missing leaves return nil. Traversal through a missing or non-table intermediate value fails safely. Gameplay access outside Active returns nil.

docs.title: Writing data
docs.text:
soul:SetData({ "Coins" }, 500)
soul:SetData({ "Stats", "Level" }, 10)
soul:SetData({ "Inventory" }, { "Sword", "Shield" })

Intermediate tables must already exist. MetaData is reserved and must not be changed by application code. SetData returns nil and warns for a value a DataStore cannot hold, or a write a DataStore would change or lose, so check its result when granting something of value.

docs.title: What can be saved
docs.text:
Strings, numbers, booleans, buffers, and tables of those. Infinity saves and comes back like any other number, and so does NaN, though SetData refuses NaN and a save warns about it.

A table is either a dictionary, with string keys, or an array, with number keys from 1. The top of a save is always a dictionary, because MetaData lives there.

Roblox goes by a table's length, #t. A table with a length is stored as an array that stops there, and every other key is lost, without an error. A table with no length is stored as a dictionary, with its number keys turned into strings. On its own, that can wipe out data:

-- On Roblox this comes back as { "Sword" }. Coins is gone, and so would be MetaData.
{ [1] = "Sword", Coins = 50 }

SoulStore protects against this in two places.

SetData refuses what would not come back the same, and returns nil:

soul:SetData({ 1 }, "Sword")                  -- a number key at the top of the save
soul:SetData({ "Inventory", 1 }, "Sword")     -- a number key on a dictionary
soul:SetData({ "Items", "Count" }, 3)         -- a string key on an array
soul:SetData({ "Levels", 1001 }, true)        -- a number key that does not start an array
soul:SetData({ "Items", 1.5 }, "Sword")       -- a fraction, zero, or a negative number
soul:SetData({ "Loadout" }, { "Sword", Name = "Main" })    -- a value with the same problems

-- Fine
soul:SetData({ "Levels", "1001" }, true)      -- number-like ids as strings
soul:SetData({ "Items", #items + 1 }, "Bow")  -- adding to an array
soul:SetData({ "Items", 2 }, nil)             -- removing from an array, even from the middle

A save loses nothing, whatever it finds. The live table from GetData has no such check, and neither does a save hook's copy, so the save handles what gets through:

In the table What is written Comes back An array with gaps, such as { "Sword", nil, "Bow" } The array, with its gaps The same, with no warning Number keys alongside string keys, at any depth Everything, with the number keys as strings Under string keys, so t[1] becomes t["1"] Number keys too sparse to be an array, such as { [1] = "a", [2000] = "b" } The same Under string keys Fractions, zero and negative numbers as keys The same Under string keys

Whatever will not come back the same gets a warning once per session, naming the table. Fix the code that wrote it: nothing was lost, but your game will not find it where it put it. See Edge Cases for more.

docs.title: Table references
docs.text:
GetData returns live table references for compatibility. Copy a table before changing it if listeners need a reliable old value:

local inventory = SoulStore.deepCopy(soul:GetData({ "Inventory" }))
table.insert(inventory, "New Item")
soul:SetData({ "Inventory" }, inventory)

Direct table mutation bypasses listeners and state guards. Do not retain data references across a yielding operation without rechecking session readiness. The final snapshot is captured when Ending begins, so later reference mutations do not change the final save.

docs.title: Reconciliation
docs.text:
Reconcile recursively fills missing fields on Active data, copying inserted tables and preserving existing values:

if soul:LoadData() then
    soul:Reconcile({
        Coins = 0,
        Level = 1,
        PremiumCurrency = 0,
    })
end

Only string keys are filled. An array the save already has is left as it is, even an empty one, so an entry the player no longer has does not come back and one entry never picks up another's fields. A missing array is copied whole:

-- Saved: { Slots = { 9 }, Sold = {} }
soul:Reconcile({ Slots = { 1, 2, 3 }, Sold = { "Starter" }, Items = { "Starter" } })
-- Result: { Slots = { 9 }, Sold = {}, Items = { "Starter" } }

Inside SetOnLoad, migrate the callback's data argument directly. The soul is still Pulling and gameplay methods are unavailable.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text: Roblox data stores fail in ways that are easy to miss. This page lists the known ones, what SoulStore does about each, and where the case comes from. Every row has a test in tests/edgecases.luau, tests/lifecycle.luau or tests/consumers.luau. The tests run against a simulated data store, and tests/studio/DataStoreProbe.server.luau checks its rules against real data stores. Where this page disagrees with older forum posts, the probe is why.

docs.title: Clocks
docs.text:
Servers can disagree about the time, by up to five minutes according to one report. In the one test that measured it, a Studio machine was 9.5 seconds off Roblox's own timestamps.

Case What SoulStore does A writer's clock is slow, so its live lock looks old Lock age comes from Roblox's UpdatedTime, not the writer's clock A reader's clock is slow, so a dead lock looks new A load that has watched a lock for all of SESSION_EXPIRY takes it, however new it looks A server's clock jumps forward or back Autosaves use os.clock, so it does not stop them A reader's clock is far ahead It reads a live lock as expired, and can take it after TAKEOVER_DELAY, between the owner's autosaves. The old session's next write is refused, so nothing is overwritten, but what it had not saved yet is lost. It takes a clock about 2 minutes off, and that player loading on a second server while the first still holds them

docs.title: Budgets and throttling
docs.text: Case What SoulStore does Source The request budget runs out Autosaves wait for budget, and only as many start as it allows. Whoever has waited longest goes first, so nobody is left behind while others save again Limits, outside review Saves bunching up after a stall, which would copy every player's data in one frame No more than twice the steady rate starts in one second The request queue fills, which drops requests with error 304 Final saves are never held back, and a dropped one retries Limits A save too large to write every 30 seconds, since each key is limited to 4 MB per minute Throttled writes fail like any other. The session stays active and the final save retries Limits Many players load at once Autosaves are spread over the whole interval, as Roblox's own sample does, and stay spread Best practices, Player data

See the rules for leave handlers Probe player.Parent is nil by the time deferred work runs A session does not depend on it, so the final hook can still read the session Probe

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: Case What SoulStore does Source A hook errors or yields That copy is not written. A final save writes the session without the hook A hook calls SaveData or LoadData, on this soul or another, which would wait inside a thread that is cancelled for waiting, and strand the session in Ending with its lock held Refused with CalledFromHook, and the save that ran the hook carries on. SaveData(true) in SetOnLoad still cancels the load, since that needs no waiting Outside review

docs.title: What only your game can do
docs.text:
Check LoadData. A load can fail for good, so don't start gameplay without checking it.

React when a session ends during play. SoulStore stops accepting changes but does not kick the player. Migrating has an example.

Record purchases in the save. Follow Roblox's steps: check the purchase id, grant, record the id, then return PurchaseGranted only if SaveData() returned true. If the save failed, the retry finds the id and saves again without granting twice.

Save before a teleport. Call SaveData(true) and wait for it, so the destination does not have to wait for the lock. If the teleport fails, start a new session.

Save both sides of a trade. Session locking stops a player loading old data, but one side of a trade can still land without the other. Call SaveData() on both, and do not treat the trade as final unless both return true.

Keep Studio away from live data. With API access on, Studio writes to real keys. Use a different store name in Studio, as your games already do.

Take a snapshot before an update that changes how data is saved. Version history only keeps the first write of each UTC hour, for 30 days. Snapshots protect what was written just before the update.

Set up right-to-erasure. SoulStore tags each key with the player's user id, and RemoveAsync leaves old versions for up to 30 days. Roblox's automated right-to-be-forgotten handles keys that follow a fixed pattern.

Keep saves well under 2 MB. At the default autosave interval, larger saves are throttled by the per-key limit on some autosaves.

Numbers above 2^53 lose precision, as they do everywhere in Luau. Store larger values as strings.

docs.title: SetOnLoad
docs.text:
Register before LoadData. The callback receives acquired data before the soul becomes Active. Mutate its argument directly: GetData, SetData, and Reconcile are gameplay methods and remain unavailable during initialization.

soul:SetOnLoad(function(data)
    if data.PremiumCurrency == nil then
        data.PremiumCurrency = 0
    end
    data.Coins = math.clamp(data.Coins or 0, 0, 1_000_000)
    if data.OldXP ~= nil then
        data.Stats = data.Stats or {}
        data.Stats.XP = data.OldXP
        data.OldXP = nil
    end
end)

local loaded, reason = soul:LoadData()
if not loaded then
    warn("Data initialization failed:", reason)
    return
end

A failed hook prevents Active gameplay. SoulStore releases the original acquired record rather than saving partial migration changes.

docs.title: SetOnSave
docs.text:
Receives a copy of the save payload. Its mutations affect that attempt only; live data is unchanged.

soul:SetOnSave(function(snapshot)
    snapshot.ActiveBoostExpiry = nil
    snapshot.TempEventData = nil
end)

A failed hook does not write its partially modified snapshot. A normal save reports the failure and the next autosave runs the hook again. A final save writes the session without the hook, so the rest of the player's progress is not lost. Transformations must be safe to run repeatedly. Keep purchases, rewards, network requests, and other external side effects outside hooks.

Both hooks must complete without yielding and must leave MetaData to SoulStore. Do not call task.wait, asynchronous APIs, or other yielding operations from them.

Saves and loads wait on the data store, so they cannot start from inside a hook, for any soul. SaveData and LoadData return false, "CalledFromHook" and warn, and the save that ran the hook carries on as usual. To end a session because of something a save hook found, do it after the hook with task.defer. One exception: SaveData(true) inside SetOnLoad cancels the load, which needs no waiting.

docs.title: Execution order
docs.text:
Acquire and load record
  -> SetOnLoad(data)
  -> Active
  -> gameplay
  -> copy save payload
  -> SetOnSave(snapshot)
  -> ownership-checked write

Ending
  -> capture final payload
  -> SetOnSave(snapshot)
  -> wait for existing writer
  -> final write and unlock together
  -> terminal event and cleanup

The final hook runs as the session starts ending, before anything yields, so nothing that runs later can change the final save. During Ending, gameplay methods reject access. Previously returned tables remain live references for compatibility, but changing them after Ending begins does not alter the captured final payload.

docs.title: When a player leaves
docs.text:
SoulStore starts the final save once every PlayerRemoving handler has run, in whatever order Roblox ran them. On Roblox the newest connection runs first, but nothing guarantees that, so do not rely on it. That leaves two rules for your own leave handlers:

  • Writing is safe. SetData and changes to the live data still work inside a leave handler, and they make the final save.
  • Do not clear what a save hook reads. The hook runs after your handler, so it would find nothing. Write it to the save in the handler instead, or clear it later with task.delay or when SessionEndBindableEvent fires.

If your own code calls SaveData(true) inside a leave handler, the final save starts right there, and handlers Roblox runs after it can no longer write.

docs.title: Change Listeners
docs.text:
:OnDataChanged() lets you react to mutations made through :SetData().

Pass nil as the path to observe the full data table. Listener paths distinguish string and number keys, including keys containing periods. Direct mutation of a GetData table does not trigger a notification.

Both values are copies, taken before and after the write, so a listener can keep them or change them without affecting the saved data. To read the current data later, use GetData or keep what the next notification brings. A nil path listener's copies leave out MetaData. Copies are only made at levels something is listening to, and they cost more the larger the table is, so prefer listening to the narrowest path you need.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
local conn = soul:OnDataChanged({ "Coins" }, function(oldValue, newValue)
    print(("Coins: %d → %d"):format(oldValue, newValue))
end)

soul:SetData({ "Coins" }, 100)
-- Output: Coins: 0 → 100

docs.title: Disconnecting
docs.text:
local conn = soul:OnDataChanged({ "Coins" }, function(old, new) end)
conn:Disconnect()

docs.title: Partial Path Matching
docs.text:
Listeners fire for every path segment a :SetData() call passes through:

soul:OnDataChanged({ "Stats" }, function(old, new)
    -- Fires when any key under "Stats" changes.
    -- old/new are the entire Stats sub-table.
end)

soul:OnDataChanged({ "Stats", "Level" }, function(old, new)
    -- Fires only for the exact "Stats.Level" key.
end)

soul:SetData({ "Stats", "Level" }, 10)
-- Both listeners above fire.

docs.title: Practical Patterns
docs.text:
Track inventory size: 

soul:OnDataChanged({ "Inventory" }, function(_, newInv)
    print("Inventory size:", #newInv)
end)

React to any stat change: 

soul:OnDataChanged({ "Stats" }, function(_, newStats)
    updateLeaderboard(player, newStats)
end)

Separate Threads

Listeners run through task.spawn; keep callbacks short. Notifications that have not started are skipped after disconnection or session end. All listener registrations are cleaned up when the soul settles.

docs.title: Load Testing
docs.text:
Edge case tests check one thing at a time. These check the ordinary day: whether everyone's data is saved consistently and fairly, at a sensible cost, when a whole game is running at once, and what happens when that game has a bad day.

Everything here was run on 2 November 2026 against version 2.0.0. Run it yourself before you rely on it, because Roblox's limits change. The session rules have changed since then: there is no lease any more, and one expiry replaces the two old settings. So the outage, crash and shutdown rows below need a new run.

docs.title: What runs
docs.text:
tests/load.luau runs a whole game through tests/fleet.luau. Each server runs its own copy of the real module against one shared data store, and players do what they do in a real game: join, load, earn things through SetData, write to the live table, buy things, hop servers, leave, and come back. Time is virtual, so hours pass in minutes.

Every write is checked as it lands, against what the data store really stored:

  • Progress never goes backwards, and SaveId goes up by exactly one.
  • Only the session holding the lock writes.
  • A save the module confirmed is never lost, and neither is a purchase made on one.
  • A player only ever loses progress if their server died.
  • Every session ends, and every lock is released, unless its server died.

The limits come from Roblox's documentation: 60 + 40 x players requests a minute for a server, 300 + 20 x players writes a minute for an experience, a queue of 30, and 4 MB of writes a minute for a key. Request times come from measuring real data stores: about 0.26 seconds, and about 30 requests a second through one server.

lune run tests/load.luau          # small enough for CI
lune run tests/load.luau large    # servers of 100 and 200 players
lune run tests/load.luau mass     # thousands of players for a simulated hour
lune run tests/load.luau large "shutting down"   # one scenario

docs.title: On the real engine
docs.text:
A simulation is only as good as its model, so tests/studio/RealFleet.luau runs a full server's worth of sessions on the real engine, against real data stores. One real Player has one key, so each session gets its own scope. A server with one player has far less budget than a real 200-player server, so these autosave every 60 seconds rather than 30, and run out of budget partway.

200 sessions, each with a save of about 17 KB, played for 5 minutes and then all ended at once:

Measure Result Loads 200 of 200, in 10.2 seconds Frames while playing 4.0 ms at the median, 7.0 ms at the 99th percentile. The worst, 110 ms, came in the first minute, as they all started Saves for purchases 149 of 150 confirmed when last counted, 0.39 seconds at the median, 1.77 at worst Final saves, all at once with the budget used up All 200 landed, in 120 seconds. With a real 200-player server's budget they would not wait for it What reached the data stores 29,800 points in all. Every record was exactly what the game had, with none missing and none still locked

tests/studio/EndToEnd.luau also passes all 199 of its checks on the real engine, including a real player leaving and a real BindToClose, and tests/studio/DataStoreProbe.server.luau finds all 53 of its rules for the fake data store still true.

What a save costs in real time on the real engine, which is the part that runs inside one frame:

Save Copying and checking it 2 KB 0.05 ms 17 KB 0.33 ms 115 KB 2.4 ms 580 KB 11.5 ms

Even with every player's autosave spread out, a 200-player server starts about 7 saves a second. At a typical 17 KB, that is about 2 milliseconds of work a second. No more than twice that steady rate starts in any one second, so a backlog cannot land all at once.

docs.title: Against ProfileStore
docs.text:
tests/compare.luau runs the same game on the real ProfileStore, through the same fleet, the same data store and the same failures, and used the way its tutorial says. ProfileStore is a strong module, and this is not a verdict on it. Its own default is to autosave every 5 minutes where SoulStore autosaves every 30 seconds, so it also ran at 30 seconds, to show what comes from that choice and what does not.

All of these ran 12 servers of 100 players, or 4 servers of 200 for the shutdown, for a simulated half hour.

Measure SoulStore ProfileStore ProfileStore at 30 seconds Healthy game: progress lost 0 of 844,129 0 of 844,510 0 of 844,717 Healthy game: requests a player a minute 2.30 0.56 2.38 Healthy game: seconds between saves, median / worst 30 / 31 185 / 251 28 / 34 Crashes: progress lost 0.39% 2.52% 0.38% Crashes: worst load, waiting for a dead server's lock 97 s 47 s 48 s Hopping servers: load at the 99th percentile 7.5 s 6.0 s 6.0 s Every server shutting down: progress lost, worst final save 0, 7 s 0, 7 s 0, 7 s 1 in 5 requests failing: worst load, worst final save 38 s, 30 s 52 s, 16 s 52 s, 52 s 2 and 10 minute outages: progress lost 0 0, but see below 0 One save a second: worst wait for a save 136 s 309 s 432 s The experience out of write budget: progress lost, worst wait for a save 0, 300 s 0, 278 s 11, 1,482 s A game writing odd tables: writes that lost named fields 0 16,534 73,783

Where the difference is the autosave interval. Crash losses and requests are simply two sides of that one setting. Given the same interval, the two lose about the same in a crash, and use about the same number of requests. ProfileStore's default costs a quarter of the requests and risks up to 5 minutes of play, and SoulStore's costs about a tenth of what Roblox allows an experience and risks about 30 seconds. Set AUTO_SAVE_INTERVAL to whichever suits your game.

Where ProfileStore is better. After a crash, its load gets in twice as fast, because it asks the owner through MessagingService and takes the lock after 40 seconds. It also has things SoulStore does not: reading old versions of a save to restore them, messages to offline players, and error signals to build monitoring on.

Where SoulStore is better. Autosaves watch the request budget, and whoever has waited longest goes first, so they stay fair when budget is tight. A long outage cannot lose a final save to the race for the lock: with the outage earlier in a smaller run, ProfileStore's default lost 0.95% when locks passed its 630 second limit, and SoulStore lost none. SoulStore had this same problem until these tests found it, and now watches even an old lock long enough for its owner's final save to land. Odd tables cannot cost the player anything. ProfileStore's documentation tells you not to write those tables, which is fair, but one stray [1] on Profile.Data loses every named field in it, and that is a mistake a game can make. SaveData also tells the caller whether the write landed, and SetData and OnDataChanged are built in.

docs.title: What the developer forum warns about
docs.text:
What developers report What SoulStore does Shown by A failed load is treated as a new player, and defaults overwrite the real save Defaults are only used when the data store answers that there is no record 1 in 5 requests failing: 0 lost A player who leaves before their data has loaded has it reset A load in progress is cancelled, and nothing is saved tests/lifecycle.luau, and the short sessions in every scenario A fast leave and rejoin loads old data The new session waits for the old session's final save, usually for less than a second Hopping servers: 0 lost, no takeovers PlayerRemoving and BindToClose both saving, which uses up the budget One final save per session, however many things ask for it Every server shutting down: 0 lost BindToClose does not run when a server crashes Autosaves bound the loss Crashes: about 35 seconds of play at most Too little time to save everyone at shutdown Final saves run side by side, inside the 30 seconds 200-player servers: 7 seconds at worst Calls that never return, with no error A later save waits at most 10 seconds behind one, and shutdown still ends on time Requests hanging: 0 lost A crashed server holds its lock forever A lock that stops changing is taken over Crashes: 97 seconds at worst Mixed tables lose data, and arrays with gaps behave inconsistently SetData refuses them, and a save loses nothing Odd tables: 0 lost Every server saving on the same schedule Each player's autosaves are spread over the whole interval Busiest second on a 200-player server: 24 requests Retries with no backoff or jitter They start at 2 seconds, as Roblox's own sample does, grow to 30, and vary by 20% tests/lifecycle.luau

Roblox's own sample autosaves every 180 seconds, and its guidance leaves that up to you. Forum advice mostly runs from 30 seconds to a minute.

docs.title: What this does not prove
docs.text:
• It is a simulation. The limits and timings are Roblox's, but the failures are the ones someone thought of. Roblox also throttles by how it splits data into partitions internally, which nothing here models.
  • Only one real server has run this at once. Real handoffs between real servers have only been simulated. Try a real server hop and a real shutdown in a test universe before you move a live game over.
  • The real test ran in Studio, which has its own limits, and real outages have not been tested at all.
  • Nothing here watches your live game. SoulStore warns in the output, but it has no signal to build alerts on. Use Roblox's observability dashboard, and practise restoring a save from its versions before you need to.

docs.title: Migrating from 1.x
docs.text: The save format is unchanged, so existing saves load without a migration. Drain old servers when you release, because old pending writes cannot enforce the new per-session ownership.

docs.title: From 2.0.0 to 2.0.1
docs.text: An outage no longer ends a session, so the end reasons LeaseExpired and ShutdownTimeout are gone. SESSION_EXPIRY replaces SESSION_LOCK_EXPIRY and LOCK_TAKEOVER_TIME, and SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT is gone, because shutdown now runs until every session has settled or Roblox ends the server.

docs.title: Arguments that changed
docs.text:
scope is now the second argument. Pass nil to keep using the same data as before.

1.x 2.0 SoulStore.new(id, player, defaults) SoulStore.new(id, nil, player, defaults) SoulStore.getSoul(id, player) SoulStore.getSoul(id, nil, player) SoulStore.resetData(id, key) SoulStore.resetData(id, nil, key) SoulStore.resetAllData(id) SoulStore.resetAllData(id, nil)

An old-style call fails safely with a warning: new and getSoul return nil, and resetData deletes nothing.

Every other function and method keeps its name and arguments.

docs.title: Same call, different behaviour
docs.text: Call What changed LoadData() Returns true, or false and a reason. Stops on corrupt data or an error retrying cannot fix, instead of retrying forever. SaveData() Makes one attempt and returns the result. In 1.x it retried until the write landed, which blocked the caller. SaveData(true) Also returns the result. Retries with growing delays. GetData, SetData, Reconcile Refused once the session starts ending. Check for nil. SetData Refuses values a data store cannot hold, NaN, and MetaData paths, and writes a data store would change or lose, such as a number key on a dictionary. Use string keys for number-like ids: tostring(level). See What can be saved. A path through a non-table returns nil instead of throwing. Leaving SoulStore's own final save now runs after every other PlayerRemoving handler, so what they write is saved. See When a player leaves. Reconcile Copies the tables it inserts, so players never share a template's table. Only fills string keys: in 1.x a saved { 9 } with a template of { 1, 2, 3 } became { 9, 2, 3 }, and now it stays { 9 }. If you add a new entry to a default array and every player should get it, add it in SetOnLoad. OnDataChanged The new value is now a copy, like the old value. In 1.x it was the live table, so a listener could change saved data through it, and anything it kept would change later. Code that keeps it should take the copy from each notification, as it fires for every SetData below the path, or read with GetData. SetOnLoad The hook works on a copy and must not yield. If it errors or yields, the load fails and the stored record is untouched. SetOnSave The hook must not yield. If it errors or yields, that copy is not written. getSoul Only returns an Active session. new Returns nil during shutdown, while the same Player instance's previous session is still ending, or for defaults that could not be saved. Waiting for a lock A lock with no write for 2 minutes can be taken over, instead of waiting out the full 5 minutes. A load first waits 15 seconds to see that it does not change, so an owner that outlived an outage can land its final save first. A healthy session keeps writing, so this does not affect it. Saving from a hook SaveData and LoadData called inside a hook return false, "CalledFromHook". See Lifecycle Hooks. Saving odd tables In 1.x a table with both [1] and string keys lost its string keys when saved, and at the top of a save that lost everything. Now nothing is lost: the number keys are saved as strings, with a warning. An array with gaps now always comes back whole.

docs.title: Check these in your game
docs.text:
Do not compare SessionId with game.JobId. MetaData.SessionId is now a token for one session, not a server id, so that comparison is always false. Check the result of SaveData instead:

-- Before
return finished and meta.SaveId > saveIdBefore and meta.SessionId == game.JobId

-- After
local saved = soul:SaveData(false)
return saved

Check the result of LoadData. A load can now fail for good, so do not start gameplay without checking it:

local loaded, reason = soul:LoadData()
if not loaded then
    warn("Player data unavailable:", reason)
    return
end

Make sure save hooks do not yield. A yielding SetOnSave hook now fails every normal save. A final save writes the session without it.

React when a session ends during play. If a session loses its record, SoulStore stops accepting changes but does not kick the player. Connect to SessionEndBindableEvent, or the player keeps playing with progress that cannot be saved:

soul.SessionEndBindableEvent.Event:Connect(function(_state, reason)
    if player.Parent == Players and reason == "OwnershipLost" then
        player:Kick("Your data session ended. Please rejoin.")
    end
end)

Update tests that load SoulStore directly. The module now has child modules, which it requires with script.Parent, and methods no longer live on the module table. SoulStore.Reconcile(soul, data) is now soul:Reconcile(data).

docs.title: Kept for existing code
docs.text: LoadState and SaveState keep their old strings, so checks such as soul.LoadState ~= "Loaded" and soul.SaveState == "Saving" still work. soul.Data is still the live table, and extra MetaData fields such as a purchase marker still round-trip.

docs.title: Resetting Data
docs.text:
Danger

Both reset functions permanently delete DataStore data. There is no undo.

docs.title: Reset a Single Player
docs.text:
SoulStore.resetData("PlayerData", nil, tostring(player.UserId))

The second argument is the DataStore scope; nil uses Roblox's default. Calls RemoveAsync on the given key, warns on failure, and returns whether it succeeded. Refused while this server has a session for that key.

When to use:

  • Clearing a QA tester's data between test runs.
  • Admin command to reset a specific player's progress by request.
  • Removing a known corrupted key.

If the player has a session on another server, that session ends with OwnershipLost on its next save and does not bring the record back. RemoveAsync leaves old versions readable through version history for up to 30 days, so a right-to-erasure request should also go through Roblox's automated process.

docs.title: Reset an Entire DataStore
docs.text:
SoulStore.resetAllData("PlayerData", nil)

This function:

  1. Refuses if this server has a session in the DataStore. Outside Studio, it also refuses unless the third argument repeats the DataStore name.
  2. Logs a warning block and waits 10 seconds before starting.
  3. Pages through all keys using ListKeysAsync.
  4. Calls RemoveAsync on each key sequentially, retrying up to five times, and stops early if a key cannot be removed.
  5. Logs a completion message and returns whether every key was removed.

Requirements:

  • Run in Roblox Studio — not on a live server.
  • No active player sessions in the target DataStore, on any server.
  • Do not close Studio or interrupt the script during the operation.

No Cancel Mechanism

The only safety net is the 10-second delay. Once the loop begins it cannot be stopped from within the script.

docs.title: Safe Usage Pattern
docs.text:
Guard all reset calls behind a Studio-only check:

local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

if RunService:IsStudio() then
    -- Uncomment exactly one:
    -- SoulStore.resetData("PlayerData", nil, "123456789")
    -- SoulStore.resetAllData("PlayerData", nil)
end

Run via the Studio command bar or a Script with RunContext = Legacy.

docs.title: Identity and lifecycle
docs.text:
SoulStore separates three identities:

Identity Use UserId Persisted DataStore key, encoded as a string. Exact Player instance Live object lookup within a DataStore and scope. GUID SessionToken Ownership stored in MetaData.SessionId.

Each rejoin creates a fresh Player instance, soul, and token. An old soul can finish saving while a new soul waits for its lock. The old object is never handed to the new Player.

Pulling -> Active -> Ending -> Ended
Pulling -> Cancelled

Pulling souls are cached to prevent duplicate acquisitions, but are unavailable through getSoul and gameplay methods. Concurrent LoadData calls share one acquisition. Gameplay starts only when LoadData returns true.

docs.title: Acquisition and writes
docs.text:
UpdateAsync atomically loads the record and claims its lock. A foreign live lock causes retry while the player remains present. An already-owned token is recognized when retrying after an uncertain network response.

Every save verifies that the persisted record names its exact token. A missing or foreign owner cancels the write, whether the record is locked, released, or expired: those only decide whether a new session may claim it. Returning from UpdateAsync without an API error does not by itself mean the save was accepted.

Normal saves make one attempt and report the result, because the next autosave carries newer data anyway. Only the final save retries.

Ending immediately blocks gameplay access and captures the final snapshot. Writers are serialized, so the final save waits behind an in-flight regular save. The same UpdateAsync writes the final data and clears Locked and SessionId. The lock is never released in advance of that write.

Departure during pulling cancels loading. If acquisition commits while cancellation is happening, SoulStore releases the acquired record without making it Active. PlayerRemoving targets the exact departing Player instance.

If the acquisition response failed and ownership is uncertain, cancellation probes only for its own token and releases it without acquiring a free record or refreshing the lock. Recovery retries for up to ACQUISITION_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT (30 seconds by default). If ownership cannot be resolved, the soul settles with AcquisitionUncertain and any remaining lock expires naturally. An already-submitted network request cannot be forcibly interrupted.

docs.title: Crash recovery
docs.text:
SESSION_EXPIRY (2 minutes) is the one setting for session locks. A lock can be taken once Roblox's UpdatedTime for the key says it has gone that long without a write. A live session writes every autosave, so this much silence means its server crashed or cannot reach the data store.

A load does not take an expired lock on first sight. It waits TAKEOVER_DELAY (15 seconds) and takes it only if it has not changed. After an outage every lock looks expired, and its owner may be about to land its final save, which retries at most about every 10 seconds, so the final save gets there first.

A failed request restarts that wait, because it says nothing about the owner, which may be failing the same way. A write from the owner restarts it too, and the claim only goes through on the exact version of the lock that was watched. Leaving and coming back costs nothing, because the lock's age keeps counting.

If this server's clock is slow, a lock can look newer than it is. So a load that has watched a lock for all of SESSION_EXPIRY takes it, however new it looks.

Any later write from the former owner is rejected by its token check, and that session ends with OwnershipLost. The module does not automatically kick the player. Applications can use the completion event to choose their disconnect or recovery flow.

An outage does not end a session. It stays Active and keeps accepting changes, and its next save lands once the store is back.

Keep the expiry comfortably longer than the autosave interval and expected DataStore delays. Shortening it trades faster crash recovery for a greater chance of taking over a session that is only slow.

Never allow gameplay on defaults while waiting for another session's lock. Existing malformed data is not treated as a missing save.

docs.title: Shutdown
docs.text:
BindToClose stops new sessions, cancels pending loads, and requests final saves for active sessions. Already-ending sessions remain tracked. Shutdown checks each session's state until all have settled, and keeps the server up for as long as Roblox allows, which is 30 seconds. Retries stay short during this time, which allows about seven attempts.

Network outages, hung requests, or platform termination can prevent a confirmed final save. Shutdown does not guarantee that every write succeeds; unreleased locks recover through expiry.

SessionEndBindableEvent fires once for terminal outcomes with (state, reason). Cancellation or ownership loss is completion, not proof of a successful final save.

docs.title: Updating existing servers
docs.text:
The persisted layout is unchanged: MetaData.SessionId remains a string, now containing an opaque GUID instead of JobId. Existing unlocked saves need no migration; existing locked saves remain protected until release, takeover or expiry.

Drain old servers when deploying this change. Old code cannot enforce the new lifecycle and may already have pending writes that use only JobId. All new application code must treat SessionId as opaque; log JobId separately when debugging.
